# Ethyca Documentation

> Privacy-as-Code platform documentation. Covers data mapping, consent management, privacy request fulfilment, AI governance assessments, and integrations across 100+ SaaS systems. Authored and maintained by the Ethyca engineering team.

## Overview

### What is Fides?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/

Fides (pronounced */fee-dhez/*, from Latin: Fidēs) is an open-source Privacy-as-Code platform that lets you manage, maintain, and automate privacy compliance throughout your organization.

## Platform

### Platform & Configuration
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform

Configure and manage the Fides platform, including installation, authentication, messaging, and domain management.

### Monitor stewardship
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/monitor-stewardship

Monitor stewardship extends Fides' [role-based access control](/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control) to **per-monitor ownership**: an eligible user can be assigned to one or more discovery monitors as a steward, which grants them write access to that monitor's results — staged resources, classifications, and review actions — without changing their overall role and without giving them control over the monitor's configuration.

### Calling the API
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/oauth/calling-api

The Fides API requires authentication via OAuth using a valid access token. In this document we'll walk through calling the Fides API with a valid access token and the appropriate scopes.

### Creating OAuth Clients
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/oauth/creating-clients

Because the root client's token contains all scopes, it can create new clients and new client ID/client secret pairs which can be used to create additional access tokens.

### Generating Access Tokens
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/oauth/generating-tokens

This document explains how to generate a valid OAuth token using a set of existing Fides credentials.

### API Authentication with OAuth
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/oauth/overview

The Fides API requires authentication via OAuth using a valid Access Token. In this section we'll explore how to generate a token, create additional OAuth clients and authenticate with appropriate scopes to the Fides API.

### Access token expiration
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/oauth/token-expiration

By default, access tokens expire after 11520 minutes (8 days). If you call the Fides API with an expired token, Fides will response with a `401` unauthorized response.

### Role-Based Access Controls
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control

Fides uses Role-Based Access Controls (RBAC) to manage user permissions across your organization. Users are assigned roles that grant them specific sets of permissions, ensuring that each team member has the appropriate level of access.

### Advanced RBAC
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control/advanced-rbac

Advanced RBAC is a Fides Plus feature. It requires Fides Plus to be installed and enabled.

### Separation of Duties
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control/constraints

Separation of duties constraints require [Advanced RBAC](/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control/advanced-rbac) to be enabled.

### Custom Roles
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control/custom-roles

Custom roles require [Advanced RBAC](/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control/advanced-rbac) to be enabled.

### Permissions Reference
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference

The granular permission system described here is part of [Advanced RBAC](/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control/advanced-rbac) and requires Fides Plus.

### User Role Assignments
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control/user-role-assignments

Advanced role assignment features (multiple roles, resource scoping, temporal access) require [Advanced RBAC](/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control/advanced-rbac) to be enabled.

### SSO Authentication
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/sso-authentication

This page documents how Single Sign-On (SSO) authentication works in Fides, including configuration options and behavioral rules.

### Configuring Azure AD
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/sso/oauth-azure

Follow the steps described here to configure Fides and Azure Active Directory for login. This will need to be completed in collaboration with the team that manages Azure AD at your organization.

### Configuring a custom OAuth provider
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/sso/oauth-custom

Follow the steps described here to configure Fides with a custom OAuth or OIDC provider. Use the custom provider option when your identity provider isn't natively supported by Fides (e.g. Auth0, Keycloak, PingIdentity, or an internal identity provider). This will need to be completed in collaboration with the team that manages your identity provider.

### Configuring Google Workspace
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/sso/oauth-google

Follow the steps described here to configure Fides and Google Workspace for login. This will need to be completed in collaboration with the team that manages Google Workspace at your organization.

### OAuth and OIDC Support in Fides
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/sso/oauth-oidc

Fides supports OAuth and OIDC for login for simpler user access control management in larger organizations.

### Configuring Okta
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/sso/oauth-okta

Follow the steps described here to configure Fides and Okta for login. This will need to be completed in collaboration with the team that manages Okta at your organization.

### System stewardship
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/authentication/system-stewardship

System stewardship extends Fides' [role-based access control](/platform/authentication/role-based-access-control) with **per-system ownership**: an eligible user can be assigned to one or more Systems as a Data Steward, which grants them an elevated set of permissions on those specific Systems without changing their overall role.

### Configuration
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/configuration/configuration

You can view the current configuration of your application via either the CLI or API.

### Data Flows: Fides Cloud vs. Self Hosted
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/configuration/fides-cloud-vs-self-hosted

Personal and sensitive data must be handled with the utmost care and Fides is designed to ensure this in any configuration. This page outlines the various Fides configurations and how personal data flows and where it is stored to help you select the optimum configuration for your needs. We'll briefly review the [available Fides configurations](#comparing-fides-cloud-and-self-hosted) and then a chart of [data flow for each major feature](#data-flow-by-feature).

### Properties
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/platform/configuration/properties

**Properties** represent different websites, native apps, or other digital surfaces that your organization operates. Each property can have its own privacy center, consent banners, and data subject request forms, customized with your specific branding and messaging.

## Consent Management

### Getting Started with Consent Management
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent

In this series of tutorials, you'll learn how the Data Map and Data Uses power consent, walk through configuring privacy notices, and finally configure a privacy experience for your users.

### What are Consent Signals?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/advanced/consent-signals

Consent signals are a template of how to send and receive a visitor's current consent choices between a publisher and a vendor, such as an advertiser or technology partner. Consent signals ensure a consistent and repeatable standard for sharing consent choices, or preferences between technology systems.

### Cross-device identity reconciliation
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/advanced/cross-device-identity

When users interact with your product across multiple devices — web browsers, mobile apps, connected TVs, and tablets — each device typically generates its own anonymous `fides_user_device_id`. Without identity linking, this creates fragmented consent records: the same person may appear as four separate users with conflicting privacy preferences.

### Consent Management: Fundamentals
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/fundamentals

In this tutorial, we'll briefly walk through what consent management is, how consent is served, why it's important, and how to automatically serve the approriate notices and gather consent for your users.

### Consent Form
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/fundamentals/consent-form

The **Consent Form** is a [privacy experience](/consent/concepts/fundamentals/privacy-experiences) built for US state privacy laws that grant a right to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information. It lets a visitor opt out **without identity verification**. There's no email confirmation, one-time passcode, or login step standing between the visitor and their opt-out.

### Consent Fundamentals: Methods of Consent
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/fundamentals/consent-methods

In this page, we'll review the various methods of consent and their requirements.

### Consent records
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/fundamentals/consent-records

Most privacy regulations require businesses to store a receipt, or proof that they have correctly obtained a user's consent choices and what those choices, or preferences, are. Consent records allow businesses to demonstrate they are complying with both a user's consent preferences and various privacy regulations globally based on the user's location.

### What is the difference between consent and preference management?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/fundamentals/consent-vs-preferences

Consent management and preference management are related but distinct concepts. Understanding the difference helps ensure your organization meets its legal obligations while also providing a good user experience.

### Identities
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/fundamentals/identities

When Fides stores a user's [consent records](/consent/concepts/fundamentals/consent-records), it needs to know **who** those preferences belong to. An **identity** is the piece of information that connects a person to their consent choices -- it's what allows Fides to associate a set of preferences with a specific individual and retrieve them later.

### Consent Fundamentals: Privacy Experiences
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/fundamentals/privacy-experiences

The user experience for a visitor to a website can vary substantially depending on the user's location. In some locations, the user may be presented with a banner or pop-up that asks them to explicitly provide their consent for the processing of their personal data, while in other locations a user may have the option to opt-out of the processing of their data by clicking a link somewhere on the website or app to manage their consent.

### Consent Fundamentals: Privacy Notices
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/fundamentals/privacy-notices

In this document, we'll explain what privacy notices are and how they are used in Fides.

### Where do Consent laws apply?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/regulations/consent-laws

Countries or regions which have data privacy laws continue to grow every year, however, as of last writing, processing of personal data requires consent in the following countries and regions:

URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/concepts/regulations/data-use-to-regulation-mapping

In this tutorial we'll walk through how to map Data Uses in Fides to major privacy regulations when configuring your systems.

### Configure Apple App Tracking Transparency (ATT)
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/guides/apple-att

Apple's [App Tracking Transparency](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apptrackingtransparency) (ATT) framework requires iOS apps to request explicit user permission before tracking users across apps and websites. Fides integrates with ATT natively through the Janus SDK: when the user denies the system prompt, non-exempt notices are automatically pre-populated to opt-out and their toggles are locked in the privacy experience.

URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/guides/configure-gpp-consent

Please contact your Ethyca solutions team if you require support for GPP with Fides. To learn more about GPP, read our [GPP user guide](/consent/standards/consent-iab-gpp).

### Consent Management: Configuring the Transparency and Consent Framework
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/guides/configure-tcf

This feature is enabled when Fides is provisioned for your by Ethyca's Privacy Deployment team. Please contact your Ethyca solutions team if you require support for TCF v2.2 with Fides. To learn more about TCF v2.2, read our [TCF user guide](/consent/standards/consent-iab-tcf).

### Fides Consent APIs
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/reference

Fides supports REST APIs, JavaScript APIs, and Mobile SDKs to support developers who want to integrate consent into their backend, front end, and mobile stacks.

### Consent APIs
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/reference/consent-api

This document will outline the capabilities of our developer-friendly consent APIs which enable developers to cache privacy experiences on CDNs, encode TC strings on the server, and easily check for changes in consent experiences and notifications.

### Consent API (v3)
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/reference/consent-api-v3

The Consent v3 API is the new interface for managing privacy preferences in Fides. It provides a unified set of endpoints for writing, reading, and reporting on consent data, with support for flexible [identity types](/consent/concepts/fundamentals/identities), [notice hierarchies](/consent/reference/propagation-policies), and fine-grained filtering.

### Janus SDK Mobile Documentation
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/reference/mobile-sdk

Janus SDK enables mobile applications to implement privacy consent management features with minimal development effort. The SDK is available for Android, iOS, and Flutter, providing a consistent API across platforms while respecting platform-specific conventions.

### Propagation policies
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/reference/propagation-policies

When you save privacy preferences through the [Consent API (v3)](/consent/reference/consent-api-v3), you can apply a **propagation policy** to automatically extend a user's consent choice across related [privacy notices](/consent/guides/privacy-notices). This page explains how notice hierarchies work and describes each available policy.

### Consent Management: Global Privacy Control (GPC)
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/standards/consent-gpc

Global Privacy Control (GPC) is a technical specification for transmitting an opt-out request directly from a user’s browser.

### Consent Management: IAB Global Privacy Platform (GPP)
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/standards/consent-iab-gpp

In an effort to better standardize publisher and advertiser data privacy compliance, the IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) developed the Global Privacy Platform, a standard framework and consent signal intended to provide compliance for General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), and Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA).

### Consent Management: IAB Multi-State Privacy Agreement (MSPA)
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/standards/consent-iab-mspa

The Multi-State Privacy Agreement (MSPA) is an updated legal framework to support the growing number of US state privacy laws. The MSPA is designed to work with the Global Privacy Platform in order to simplify compliance for publishers by obtaining, collecting and signaling consent for publishers to advertisers using a standard contractual framework that directly supports the legal requirements of the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA), as well as the Colorado Privacy Act (CPA), Connecticut Data Privacy Act (CTDPA), Utah Consumer Privacy Act (UC

### Consent Management: IAB TCF Explained
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/standards/consent-iab-tcf

The IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) Transparency & Consent Framework (TCF) is a [consent signal](/consent/concepts/advanced/consent-signals) and framework that was jointly developed by the publishing, advertising, and online services industries to give users granular control over their data while ensuring the industry could publish content and supply advertising backed services at scale.

### Consent Management: IAB TCF Explained
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/standards/consent-iab-tcf-ca

IAB TCF may be primarily thought of as a requirement for consent in Europe under the GDPR, however IAB Canada has established a separate version of TCF to support the specific requirements of Canadian Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA).

### IAB TCF Library Update, May 2025
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/standards/consent-iab-tcf/tcf-library-update-may-2025

The IAB has announced a mandatory update to the TCF TypeScript Library (iabtcf-es) that changes how vendor legitimate interests are encoded in the TC String. This update affects all users of the IAB library, including our platform which uses this library internally.

### Consent Management: IAB USPrivacy Explained
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/consent/standards/consent-iab-usp

Similar to the IAB TCF in Europe, the USPrivacy string was established by the IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) initially in response to the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).


## Privacy Requests

### Getting Started with Privacy Requests
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests

In this series of tutorials, you'll configure integrations for processing privacy requests for your systems and walk through the steps to test a privacy request to check for issues that may occur in the request process.

### Data Rights Protocol
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/concepts/data-rights-protocol

The [Data Rights Protocol](https://github.com/consumer-reports-digital-lab/data-rights-protocol) (DRP) is a technical standard for exchanging data rights requests under regulations like the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).

### Privacy Request Execution
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/concepts/execution

Fully configured, Fides provides end-to-end [privacy request](/privacy-requests) execution. The following outline summarizes the steps Fides takes to fulfill privacy requests, including optional configurations and manual data retrieval.

### Privacy Requests: Fundamentals
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/concepts/fundamentals

This page introduces the key terms and concepts behind privacy requests. For detailed guides on each topic, follow the links below.

### Query Execution
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/concepts/graphs

Fides uses your Datasets to generate a _graph_ of the resources. Based on the identity data you provide, Fides then generates a specific _traversal_, which is the order of steps that will be taken to fulfill a specific request.

### Privacy Request Overview
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/concepts/overview

A privacy request represents an ask from a user to perform an action on their identity data. The request itself identifies the user by email address, phone number, social security number, or other identifiable information. The data that will be affected, and how it's affected, is described in a privacy request policy associated with the request.

### Overview: Privacy requests
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides

In this guide, we'll walk through what a privacy request is and how to get started receiving, managing and processing incoming privacy requests.

### Annotate Complex Fields
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/complex-fields

Fides can retrieve and mask data from complex objects and arrays. This involves annotating your dataset files to let Fides know about your complex data.

### Configuring Privacy Requests
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/configuration

In this tutorial, we'll walk through how to configure a privacy request in Fides.

### Configuring Datasets
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/configuration/configuring-datasets

This guide walks you through the process of editing and testing datasets in Fides. Datasets are the foundation of your privacy request system, defining the structure and relationships of your data. You'll learn how to edit, validate, and connect datasets to ensure they accurately represent your data model and support your privacy operations.

### Privacy Requests: Configuring Databases
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/configuration/databases

In this tutorial, you'll configure a privacy request integration for a database. By the end of this tutorial, you'll understand the relationship between systems, integrations, datasets, and databases as well as how to connect, configure and test an integration.

### Privacy Requests: Configuring Integrations
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/configuration/integrations

In this tutorial, you'll add and configure a privacy request integration for a system on the [Data Map.](/data-mapping) By the end of this tutorial, you'll understand the relationship between systems and integrations as well as how to connect, configure, and test an integration.

### Configuring Email Templates
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/configure-email

When managing privacy requests, it's important to keep consumers informed about the progress of their requests. This is typically managed through email templates, which can be customized both in terms of content (continue reading) and [appearance](/privacy-requests/guides/configure-email/email-style). The following instructions outline how to modify the email content for each request type.

### Email Style Customizations
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/configure-email/email-style

In order to implement custom styling for email templates, Fides supports forwarding [variables](/privacy-requests/guides/configure-email/email-template-types) directly to an email provider like Mailgun, Sendgrid, or Twilio. In this tutorial, we are going to walk through an example of using [Mailgun](/platform/messaging/mailgun-email) to style an email.

### Email Template Types
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/configure-email/email-template-types

The following types of emails may be sent while processing privacy requests: * [Subject identify verification](#subject-identity-verification): An email used to confirm the identity of a data subject. * [Privacy request received](#privacy-request-received): An email sent to a data subject when a privacy request has been received. * [Privacy request approved](#privacy-request-approved): An email sent to a data subject when a privacy request has been approved. * [Privacy request denied](#privacy-request-denied): An email sent to a data subject when a privacy request has been denied, including th

### Overview
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/custom-identities

This document explains how to configure configure custom identities that will be collected for privacy requests.

### Overview
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/custom-request-fields

Custom request fields let you collect extra information from data subjects when they file a privacy request — for example, a state of residence, supporting documents, or the reason behind the request.

### Attachments
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/custom-request-fields/attachments

A `file` field lets the data subject attach supporting documents (for example, proof of identity) when submitting a privacy request. This page covers both adding a file field to your intake form and enabling file uploads in your Fides deployment.

### Conditional Display and Validation
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/custom-request-fields/conditional-display-validation

Any custom field can be gated on the value of another field in the same intake form by adding a `display_condition` rule. The Privacy Center evaluates the rule against the values the data subject has entered so far and only renders the dependent field when the rule resolves to `true`.

### Configuration
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/custom-request-fields/configuration

This page explains how to enable custom request fields and add them to your Privacy Center intake form using JSON configuration.

### Form Builder
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/custom-request-fields/form-builder

The form builder lets you visually design the intake form that data subjects see when they submit a privacy request — no JSON editing required. You can add fields, configure their properties, set up conditional visibility rules, reorder fields with drag-and-drop, and preview the form as the end user will see it.

### Privacy Requests: Identifying & Debugging Issues
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/debugging

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to review the event logs for a privacy request and identify issues that may require debugging.

### Duplicate DSR detection
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/duplicate-detection

Fides can automatically detect and suppress duplicate Data Subject Requests (DSRs). When enabled, any new privacy request that matches an existing one — same identity, same request type, within a configured time window — is automatically labeled **Duplicate** and skipped without processing.

### Subject Identity Verification
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/identity-verification

When you receive a privacy request, you are responsible for confirming the identity of the subject to ensure that you do not incorrectly disclose data. To verify an identity, you may only request additional information you already retain about the subject. For example, you can't request a copy of a subject's drivers license if you don't already have this information.

### Configure Data Masking
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/masking-strategies

Data masking is the process of obfuscating data in client systems, so it is no longer recognizable as PII (personally identifiable information).

### Configure Pre-Approval Webhooks
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/pre-approval-webhooks

A pre-approval webhook is an HTTPS callback that calls an external REST API endpoint as soon as a privacy request is received (or after user identity verification, if that is configured).

### Processing privacy requests
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/processing-requests

Privacy request processing is the process by which approved privacy requests are submitted to internal database or third party SaaS applications to be fulfilled. Said differently, processing is the execution of the privacy request that ensures that the legal obligation has been fulfilled.

### Properties
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/properties

**Properties** represent different websites, native apps, or other digital surfaces that your organization operates. Each property can have its own privacy center, consent banners, and data subject request forms, customized with your specific branding and messaging.

### Privacy Request Redaction Patterns
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/redaction-patterns

The Privacy Request Redaction Patterns feature allows administrators to automatically mask sensitive dataset, collection, and field names in DSR (Data Subject Request) package reports. This helps protect sensitive information while still providing useful reports for compliance and debugging purposes.

### Report on Privacy Requests
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/reporting

The reporting feature allows you to fetch information about privacy requests. You can opt for high-level status information, or get more detailed information about the status of the requests on each of your collections.

### Managing privacy requests
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/reviewing-requests

Once privacy requests have been [submitted](/privacy-requests/guides/submitting-requests), they must be reviewed.

### Configure Storage Destinations
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/storage-destinations

Data subject access requests (DSARs) produce a package of returned data upon completion. This data is then uploaded to a storage destination (e.g. an S3 bucket) before being sent to the user.

### Submitting privacy requests
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/submitting-requests

Data subjects have several rights when it comes to the protection and processing of their personal data. These rights may vary depending on the specific data protection regulations applicable in a given jurisdiction, such as the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). But, here are some commonly recognized rights:

### Configure Privacy Request Webhooks
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/guides/webhooks

A privacy request webhook is an HTTPS callback that you've defined on an [execution policy](/privacy-requests/reference/request-policies) to trigger an external REST API endpoint either *before* or *after* a privacy request executes.

### Privacy Requests: Glossary
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/reference/glossary

Looking for a general privacy, data protection, or AI governance term? See the [Ethyca Glossary](https://ethyca.com/glossary). This page lists terms specific to Fides Privacy Requests.

### Privacy request annotations
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/reference/privacy-request-annotations

When Fides processes privacy requests, it needs to know how to traverse your datasets to process all data related to the user. This is done by creating references across datasets.

### Configure DSR Request Policies
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-requests/reference/request-policies

A DSR request policy (separate from a [CI Policy](/cli-reference/check), used for automated policy checks in CI) is a set of instructions, or Rules, that are executed when a user submits a [request](/privacy-requests) to retrieve or delete their data. It describes how to access, mask, or erase data that matches specific data categories in submitted privacy requests.


## Data Mapping

### Getting Started with Data Mapping
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping

In this series of tutorials, you'll add a new system manually to your data map and use Fides' Detection Scanners. You'll update your system's privacy activities, view your system on the data map and export a compliance report.

### Monitors
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/concepts/discovery-monitor

Fides **monitors** help you stay up-to-date as data architecture changes in your organization that impact your privacy and governance programs.

### Data Mapping: Fundamentals
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/concepts/fundamentals

In this tutorial we will briefly walk through what a data map is, why they are important and, how to efficiently build and maintain your data map.

### Data Mapping: Adding Systems Manually
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/adding-systems-manually

In this tutorial, you'll add a new system manually to your data map. By the end of this tutorial, you'll understand systems and data maps, and how to manage them in Fides.

### Asset Report
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/asset-report

The Asset Report provides a comprehensive, cross-system view of all discovered assets in your data map. Assets include cookies, JavaScript tags, images/pixels, iFrames, and browser requests that have been detected across your systems through automated scanning or manual documentation.

### Assigning monitor stewards
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/assigning-monitor-stewards

Assigning stewards to a discovery monitor scopes the day-to-day discovery work — promoting staged resources, approving classifications, working the Action Center — to a specific set of users without granting them control over the monitor's configuration.

### Data mapping: selecting vendors
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/choosing-vendors

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to select vendors to add as systems in the data map, using [Fides Compass](/data-mapping/guides/compass) to populate all system information. This will get you started quickly so that you can configure privacy requests and consent.

### Fides Compass: a privacy intelligence dictionary
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/compass

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to use Fides Compass, a privacy dictionary, to autocomplete system and data use information. By the end of this tutorial, you'll understand how to specify a vendor profile and retrieve suggestions from the dictionary.

### Confidence Scores
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/confidence-scores

When the Fides LLM classifier tags a field with a data category, it also returns a **confidence rating** — a 1–5 integer reflecting how certain it is about the predicted classification. These ratings are grouped into **confidence buckets** (High, Medium, Low, or Manual) that surface in the Action Center and Schema Explorer to help you prioritize your review.

### Data Lineage
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/data-lineage

Data Lineage is a visual map of the systems in your organization and the data flows between them. The view is built from the same system inventory that powers the Data Map report; any system, added via [monitoring](/integrations/identity-providers) or [manually](/data-mapping/guides/adding-systems-manually), appears here automatically.

### Data mapping annotations
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/data-mapping-annotations

Data mapping annotations categorize user and system data, permitting Fides to access or delete user data for a DSR.

### Data Mapping: Monitoring Data Sources
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/data-monitor

Fides Detection & Discovery (D&D) tracks the updates to your organization’s data architecture. When a data source is updated, Fides will report the added, removed, or changed fields as well as suggest data categorizations for those fields.

### Data Mapping: Data Use & Processing Activities
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/data-uses

In this tutorial, you'll add your system's privacy activities and by the end of this tutorial, you'll be able to update and manage your system's privacy and processing activities for reporting.

### Helios
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/helios

After completing a **Scan**, **staged resources** appear in the *Action center*. Choose which monitor should be reviewed, within the *Attention required* tab. In-progress tasks can be viewed in the *Activity* tab. After a monitor is selected, the **Schema explorer** provides a tree navigation to review child assets of the **staged resource**.

### LLM Classification Configuration
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/llm-classification

Fides' Data Discovery module includes an LLM-powered data classifier that leverages large language models to automatically identify and categorize sensitive data in your systems. This guide explains how to configure AWS Bedrock as the LLM backend for Fides' data classification capabilities.

### Viewing and editing the taxonomy
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/managing-taxonomy

In this guide, you'll learn how to view your different taxonomy classification groups (Data Categories, Data Uses, and Data Subjects), edit individual labels, add new taxonomy labels, and delete unwanted labels.

### Data Mapping: Reporting
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/reports

In this tutorial, you'll explore your Data Map, filter the Map and Table views, and export a report. By the end of this tutorial you will be familiar with Fides' Data Map visualizations, filters and report exports.

### Reviewing system history
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/review-history

In this guide, we will describe how to use the System History tab in the UI to review and audit changes that have been made to systems in the data map.

### Data Mapping: Automated System Detection
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/guides/system-detection

In this tutorial, you'll add a new system to your data map using Fides' Discovery Scanners. By the end of this tutorial, you'll understand, and be able to use Fides' various detection tools to discover systems in your cloud host and single sign-on providers as well as low-level network dataflow analysis.

### Classifier Parameters
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/reference/classification

Fides classification leverages several named-entity recognition Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools, leveraging Python libraries including spacy and presidio. Enterprise customers interested in AI-driven classification should inquire about the Fides classifier extension using privateAI.

### Data Mapping: Glossary
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/reference/glossary

Looking for a general privacy, data protection, or AI governance term? See the [Ethyca Glossary](https://ethyca.com/glossary). This page lists terms specific to Fides Data Mapping.

### Automate Data Store Monitor Activities
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/reference/monitor-api

**Data Store Monitors** scan databases to produce [Datasets](/data-mapping/reference/monitor-api) that are labeled with the [Fideslang](/data-mapping/guides/data-mapping-annotations#fideslang-data-categories) data privacy taxonomy.

### System History API
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/data-mapping/reference/system-history-api

Fides monitors system changes and offers an API endpoint for accessing the system history. Additionally, a digest of changes made over a 24-hour period is provided, which can be accessed via a webhook.

## Privacy Center & FidesJS

### Privacy Center & FidesJS
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs

Build and customize the user-facing components of your privacy program. The Privacy Center provides a configurable webpage for data subject requests and consent, while FidesJS delivers client-side consent management for web and mobile.

### FidesJS Documentation
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/fidesjs

Learn about FidesJS, Fides' Javascript SDK for integrating Fides into your own websites and web applications.

### Privacy Center FidesJS Hosting (`GET /fides.js`)
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/fidesjs/privacy-center-fidesjs-hosting

In a production deployment (like Fides Cloud), the [FidesJS](/privacy-center-fidesjs/fidesjs/reference/README) JavaScript bundle is hosted by your Fides Privacy Center so that it can be customized for your users when added to your website. For example, if your Privacy Center is at `https://privacy.example.com`, you might add the following script tag to your website to add FidesJS:

### GPP API
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/fidesjs/reference/gpp-api

When Fides is configured to support the IAB's [Global Privacy Platform (GPP)](/consent/standards/consent-iab-gpp), FidesJS includes the GPP API so that downstream services can call it to get a user's privacy preferences and ensure that advertising and other services are loaded according to user preferences.

### Troubleshooting
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/fidesjs/troubleshooting

This document contains typical troubleshooting questions and answers that you might run into while working with `fides.js`.

### Janus SDK Mobile Documentation
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/mobile-sdk

Janus SDK enables mobile applications to implement privacy consent management features with minimal development effort. The SDK is available for Android, iOS, and Flutter, providing a consistent API across platforms while respecting platform-specific conventions.

### Privacy Center Overview
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/privacy-center

The Fides Privacy Center is a configurable webpage where users can request to access, update, or delete their data or update their consent preferences.

### Configure Appearance
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/privacy-center/appearance

To customize the appearance of your Privacy Center, prepare a CSS stylesheet with your desired styles. You can then apply these styles in two ways:

### Adding Privacy Center Configuration to Properties
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/privacy-center/configuration

A default property is automatically created for you. You can manage your privacy center configuration through the API or by directly editing configuration files.

### Configure Consent Options
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/privacy-center/consent-options

The list of consent notices displayed to the user and their options are controlled by the _Consent_ section of the configuration file. Within this section, consent options may be defined for the privacy center page and for the resulting consent options page.

### CCPA/CPRA Disclosure Metrics
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/privacy-center/disclosure-metrics

The privacy request disclosure metrics feature provides a public-facing page in the Privacy Center that displays annual CCPA/CPRA disclosure data, as required by California Civil Code § 1798.130(a)(5) and 11 CCR § 7102.

### Multiple Privacy Centers
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/privacy-center-fidesjs/privacy-center/multiple-privacy-centers

Multiple privacy centers allows you to configure different privacy centers for different paths on the same domain or for different domains entirely. This feature requires [API-based configuration](/privacy-center-fidesjs/privacy-center/configuration#recommended-api-based-configuration).

## Integrations

### Overview: Integrations
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations

In this section, we will explore [Integrations](https://www.ethyca.com/product/privacy-request-automation/integrations), an essential element of data mapping required to process Data Subject Requests (DSRs).

### Database Integrations
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases

Fides supports a variety of database integrations for privacy request automation. Select a database below to learn about its specific configuration and capabilities.

### Google BigQuery
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases/bigquery

[Google BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/) is a fully managed, highly scalable, and serverless data warehouse and analytics platform that enables organizations to store, query, and analyze massive amounts of data with ease.

### Amazon DynamoDB
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases/dynamodb

[Amazon DynamoDB](https://www.amazonaws.cn/en/dynamodb/) is a fully managed NoSQL database service provided by Amazon Web Services (AWS) that touts seamless scalability, high availability, and low latency for handling large amounts of structured and semi-structured data.

### MariaDB
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases/mariadb

[MariaDB](https://mariadb.org/) is an open-source, relational database management system (RDBMS) that is a drop-in replacement for MySQL, offering enhanced performance, scalability, and additional features.

### MongoDB
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases/mongodb

[MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/) is a flexible and scalable NoSQL database management system that stores data in a document-oriented format, offering high performance and easy horizontal scaling.

### MS SQL Server
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases/mssql

[MS SQL Server](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/sql-server/), also known as Microsoft SQL Server, is a comprehensive relational database management system (RDBMS) developed by Microsoft, offering enterprise-level features, robust performance, and seamless integration with other Microsoft products and technologies.

### MySQL
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases/mysql

[MySQL](https://MySQL.org/) is a popular open-source relational database management system (RDBMS) known for its ease of use, scalability, and wide adoption in web applications.

### PostgreSQL
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases/postgresql

[PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) is a powerful open-source object-relational database management system (ORDBMS) known for its robustness, extensibility, and adherence to SQL standards.

### Amazon RDS PostgreSQL
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases/rdspostgresql

[RDS PostgreSQL](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/postgresql/) extends standard PostgreSQL functionality to help organizations set up, operate, and scale their solution on the cloud.

### Amazon Redshift
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases/redshift

[Amazon Redshift](https://aws.amazon.com/redshift/) is a fully managed cloud data warehousing service that offers fast query performance and scalability for analyzing large volumes of data using an SQL-based approach.

### Snowflake
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/databases/snowflake

[Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/) is a cloud-based data platform that provides a highly scalable and fully managed solution for storing, processing, and analyzing large volumes of structured and semi-structured data.

### Dynamic Erasure Email integration
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/email-integrations/dynamic-erasure-emails

A _Dynamic Erasure Email integration_ allows Fides to send a weekly email containing the identities of all the data subjects that have submitted an erasure request in the past week. _Dynamic Erasure Emails_ can be used to notify multiple third-party vendors of their obligations to erase any personal data associated with the provided identities.

### Generic Erasure Email integration
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/email-integrations/generic-erasure-emails

A _Generic Erasure Email integration_ allows Fides to send a weekly email to a generic email address of your choice, containing the identities of all the data subjects that have submitted an erasure request in the past week.

### Custom Integration Templates
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/guides/custom-integrations

Fides supports custom integration templates that can be uploaded at runtime to extend or override the built-in connector library. This feature is available to admin users from the **System > Integrations** tab.

### Datasets
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/guides/datasets

Datasets describe the schema of databases and other data stores connected to Fides. They are used to map personal data fields and configure privacy request execution.

### Create a Dataset YAML from scratch
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/guides/datasets/create-dataset-yaml

Datasets are an abstract identifier of your data store. For example, if you are working with structured tabular data, this is usually generated from a _schema_. ```yaml filename="postgres_dataset.yml" dataset: - fides_key: postgres_example_test_dataset organization_fides_key: default_organization tags: null name: Postgres Example Test Dataset description: Example of a Postgres dataset containing a variety of related tables like customers, products, addresses, etc. ```

### Editing SaaS Datasets
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/guides/datasets/edit-saas-datasets

SaaS integration datasets are automatically generated when you configure a SaaS integration. However, you may need to customize these datasets — for example, to add data categories, update field descriptions, or remove fields that are not relevant to your use case.

### Creating datasets from the CLI
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/guides/datasets/generate-datasets-cli

The ```fides push``` command allows you to quickly add YAML datasets from your working project directory to the Fides server.

### Creating Datasets in the UI
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/guides/datasets/generate-datasets-ui

Fides can generate datasets by connecting to datastores and interpreting the data structure: 1. Navigate to **Manage datasets**. 2. Click **Create new dataset**. 3. Click **Connect to a database**. 4. Paste the _database connection_ string into the `Database URL` field. 5. Click **Generate dataset**.

### Dataset integrations
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/guides/datasets/link-datasets

In this section, we will explore the process for linking datasets to [integrations](/integrations) so that privacy requests can be executed against all of your data, whether in a database or third party SaaS application.

### Datasets
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/guides/datasets/overview

Datasets are an important component for processing privacy requests. They codify your organization's data architecture using [FidesLang data categories](https://ethyca.github.io/fideslang/taxonomy/overview/) and describe the data processing activity related to each of your data stores.

### Managing integrations
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/guides/manage-integrations

In this guide, you'll learn how to:

### Identity Providers
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/identity-providers

Identity provider (IDP) monitors connect to your organization's identity platform to discover registered applications. Each discovered application appears in the Action Center for review, where you can evaluate whether it should be added to your data map.

### Entra
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/identity-providers/entra

[Microsoft Entra ID](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/business/identity-access/microsoft-entra-id) (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service. The Entra IDP monitor discovers app registrations in your Entra tenant — including their name, status, creation date, and domain — and surfaces them in the Action Center for review.

### Okta
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/identity-providers/okta

[Okta](https://www.okta.com/) is an identity and access management platform that provides single sign-on, multi-factor authentication, and user provisioning. The Okta IDP monitor discovers applications registered in Okta — such as [HubSpot](/integrations/saas-integrations/hubspot) and [Snowflake](/integrations/databases/snowflake) — and surfaces them in the Action Center for review.

### Jira manual tasks
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/manual-tasks/jira-manual-tasks

Jira manual tasks enable Fides to automatically create Jira tickets when privacy requests are approved, track their progress, and complete the associated manual task when the Jira ticket is resolved. This allows your team to manage manual privacy request fulfillment directly in Jira, using your existing workflows and project boards, rather than through the Fides admin UI alone.

### Manual Task Conditions
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/manual-tasks/manual-task-conditions

By default, manual tasks are created for each privacy request that Fides receives. While this may be appropriate for commonly used systems, there may be times when you want to limit the tasks that are created. For example, it is a privacy best practice not to expose the identifying information required to respond to a manual task to a third party if that user is not in the system. Additionally, the vendor may have requirements that you limit the requests sent to them to fulfill so as to not overwhelm their own services or processes.

### **Manual privacy request tasks**
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/manual-tasks/overview

Manual tasks provide a way to process privacy requests against systems that do not provide programmatic access or lack the APIs to process requests programmatically. While Fides aims to automate as much of the privacy request process as possible, there are often legacy systems in which data must be exported or deleted manually. Manual tasks in Fides provide a basic task management interface that allows both internal and external users to respond to and manage the specific tasks related to access and erasure requests in systems they are responsible for.

### Connection types
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/reference/database-connection-types

To view a list of all available integrations, visit `GET /api/v1/connection_type`. This endpoint can be filtered with a `search` query param or a `system_type` query param and is subject to change. We include database options and third party API services with which Fides can communicate.

### Dataset annotation reference
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/reference/dataset-annotation-reference

This page serves as a comprehensive reference for all dataset annotations available in Fides. Dataset annotations are defined in YAML and help describe your data architecture for privacy request processing.

### What is a SaaS configuration?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/saas-integrations/developer-reference/saas-config

A [SaaS connector](/integrations/saas-integrations/developer-reference/saas-config) is defined in two parts: the [Dataset](/integrations/guides/datasets), and the SaaS configuration. The Dataset describes the data that is available from the connector, and the SaaS config describes how to connect to, and retrieve or update the data in the connector.

### OAuth2
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/saas-integrations/developer-reference/saas-oauth2

SaaS integrations support two OAuth2 flows:

### SaaS pagination
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/saas-integrations/developer-reference/saas-pagination

These pagination strategies allow Fides to incrementally retrieve content from SaaS APIs. APIs can vary in the way subsequent pages are accessed so these configurable options aim to cover a majority of common use cases.

### SaaS Post-Processors
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/saas-integrations/developer-reference/saas-postprocessors

Post-processors are, in essence, data transformers. Given data from an endpoint, we can add specific processors to transform the data into a format we need for privacy requests.

### **Website integration & monitor**
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/websites/overview

The Fides website integration and monitor automates the detection of potential data privacy risks on your websites and helps streamline consent management. It scans your site to identify technologies like cookies, pixels, and tags providing detailed information about what they do and where they come from.

### **Setting up a website monitor**
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/websites/set-up

1. Navigate to the integrations view in Fides. 2. Select "Add integration." 3. Select "Configure" on the website integration option at the base of the modal. 4. Name the integration (we suggest a name that corresponds with the website you intend to scan). 5. Enter the website URL (Provide the main web address you want to monitor, typically a homepage). 6. Select "Save."

### **Taking action on monitor results**
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/websites/taking-action

The Action Center provides tools to manage the assets detected by the website monitor.

### **Understanding monitor results**
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/integrations/websites/understanding-results

The website monitor provides a comprehensive view of the tracking technologies active on your website. After a scan is complete, the results are presented in the Action Center, organized by the monitor that detected the assets. Each monitor will have its own row in the action center.

URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ccpa/gpc_ccpa

### CCPA Step 07: Providing User Right to Portability
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ccpa/portability_ccpa

### What is the CCPA?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ccpa/what_is_ccpa

### GDPR: What is it and how to comply?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr

The European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is the world's most foundational consumer data privacy law. Since going into effect in 2018, it has influenced successive global privacy laws like Brazil's LGPD and California's CPRA.

### 7 Principles of GDPR
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/7_principles_gdpr

[Article 5](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-5-gdpr/) of GDPR covers the seven core principles of privacy law your business must follow to legally collect and process the personal data of EU citizens. Implementing these principles is the first step your business should take toward GDPR compliance. This page will go over each principle in more detail.

### GDPR Step 02: Access Requests for GDPR
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/access_requests_gdpr

Under GDPR, your business must provide consumers with the ability to request access to their personal data and respond to their requests within one month. You may also request a two month extension for a legitimate reason or if a delay occurs in processing their request.

### Additional Business Obligations of GDPR
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/addtl_obligations_gdpr

Along with fulfilling consumers' subject rights requests and enabling their consent preferences, your business will need to fulfill an additional set of organizational obligations to comply with GDPR. Here are these business requirements in more detail.

### Summary
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/conclusion_gdpr

Ensuring your business complies with all GDPR requirements can feel overwhelming. Luckily, Ethyca makes it easy with the Fides privacy intelligence platform. You can also leverage the privacy engineering expertise of the [Fides open-source community](https://www.ethyca.com) to ensure that your business will be able to comply with any global privacy law.

### GDPR Step 03: Correction Requests for GDPR
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/correction_requests_gdpr

You may already be enabling consumers to correct personal information that they believe is incorrect in your business systems.

### GDPR Step 1: Creating a Data Map
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/data_map_gdpr

Producing a data map of where all of the data lies throughout your organization will help you comply with Article 30’s RoPA requirement. Not only that, your business must have full context of all the data you are processing to exercise granular control over all the data flowing through your systems.

### GDPR Step 06: Data Protection Assessments
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/dpa_gdpr

Under [Article 35](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-35-gdpr/) of GDPR, businesses must perform data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) before processing personal data. DPIAs weigh the business benefits of processing users' data with the potential risks on consumers. Going through these assessments will help your business identify any unaddressed risks of processing consumers' data.

### GDPR Step 04: Erasure Requests for GDPR
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/erasure_requests_gdpr

### GDPR Step 05: Portability Requests for GDPR
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/portability_requests_gdpr

Processing a user’s right to data portability is identical to an access request. The key difference is that the data returned to the user should be in a machine-readable format that could be transferred to another vendor or business.

### What is GDPR?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/what_is_gdpr

The [General Data Protection Regulation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32016R0679) (GDPR) is a comprehensive consumer privacy law that protects the data privacy rights of all EU citizens. If your businesses offer products or services to EU citizens and collect and process their personal data, you must comply with GDPR. You can the steps in this guide to ensure GDPR compliance.

### What are the requirements of GDPR?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gdpr/what_reqs_gdpr

### GPC: What is it and how to comply?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gpc

This tutorial is an easy to follow guide that describes what the Global Privacy Control, or GPC is, how to detect it, and how to support it for any tech stack.

### For consumers, how does GPC work?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gpc/consumer_gpc

As a first step, privacy preferences can be set by the user in their browser if that browser supports the GPC standard.

### GPC Bonus:
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gpc/dataflow_gpc

A common misconception with consent enforcement is that it relates to preventing cookies or pixels firing in your website. While this is absolutely true, it’s very important to remember that while some of your consumer’s data is transmitted to vendors from your website’s pixels and events, it is also possible that data is flowing from your back end systems and data tools.

### GPC Step 01:
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gpc/detect_gpc

In order to support the GPC, you'll need to understand how to detect the signal, appropriately record it, and process it.

### For developers, how does GPC work?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gpc/dev_gpc

As a first step, preferences are set in a user's browser. (Note: for technical purposes browsers are referred to as user agents.)

### GPC Step 03:
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gpc/enforce_gpc

In some cases, such as advertising technology and platform providers who support standards such as IAB CCPA compliance of the TCF String, these vendors will already respect an opt-out signal if shared with them.

### GPC Step 02:
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gpc/geo_gpc

While both California’s Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and Calififornia’s Privacy Rights Act (CPRA) should abide by the GPC by default, it’s important to consider whether you will afford these rights to other jurisdictions, whether that is other US states or other global jurisdications.

### For legal teams - How does my business comply with GPC?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gpc/legal_gpc

California’s Privacy Protection Agency, the [CPPA](https://cppa.ca.gov), was the first regulator to formally confirm that they expect businesses to comply with GPC as part of California privacy regulations. In demonstrating their willingness to enforce, in August 2022, [Sephora was fined $1.2M](https://iapp.org/news/a/the-sephora-case-do-not-sell-but-are-you-selling/) for not complying with data sales consent requirements including the Global Privacy Control. However, other US States, like Colorado, Connecticut, Texas, Oregon, and Montana, have indicated that they will also require compliance 

### What is the GPC?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/gpc/what_is_gpc

Global Privacy Control (GPC) is a technical specification for transmitting an opt-out request directly from a user’s browser.

### UCPA: What is it and how to comply?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ucpa

The fifth and final privacy law going into effect this year is the Utah Consumer Privacy Act (UCPA). Utah’s privacy law will go into effect at the end of the year on December 31, 2023.

### UCPA Step 02: Access Requests for UCPA
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ucpa/access_requests_ucpa

Under UCPA, your business must provide consumers with the ability to request access to their personal data and respond to their requests within 45 days. You may also request a 45-day extension for a legitimate reason or if a delay occurs in processing their request.

### Additional Business Obligations of UCPA
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ucpa/addtl_reqs_ucpa

Utah privacy law also includes specific business obligations that your company must follow to achieve compliance. The business obligations UCPA mandates are fewer in scope than other state privacy laws. For example, UCPA does not require businesses to conduct Data Protection Assessments.

### Conclusion
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ucpa/conclusion_ucpa

Utah’s privacy law is the last of the five U.S. state privacy regulations going into effect in 2023. Leveraging the privacy engineering expertise of the [Fides open-source community](https://www.ethyca.com), as well as the Fides privacy intelligence platform, will ensure that your business will be able to comply with any global privacy law.

### UCPA Step 1: Creating a Data Map
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ucpa/data_map_ucpa

While a data map is not an explicit requirement under Utah’s privacy law, a data map is the foundation for privacy compliance. Your business must have full context of all the data you are processing to exercise granular control over all the data flowing through your systems.

### UCPA Step 04: Erasure Requests for UCPA
