### UCPA Step 04: Portability Requests for UCPA
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ucpa/portability_ucpa

Processing a user’s right to data portability is identical to an access request. The key difference is that the data returned to the user should be in a machine-readable format that could be transferred to another vendor or business.

### What is the UCPA?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ucpa/what_is_ucpa

[The Utah Consumer Privacy Act (UCPA)](https://le.utah.gov/~2022/bills/sbillenr/SB0227.pdf) is a comprehensive consumer privacy law that protects the data privacy rights of all Utah residents. UCPA will go into effect at the end of the year on December 31, 2023. If your business is subject to Utah’s privacy law, you can the steps in this guide to ensure UCPA compliance.

### What are the requirements of the UCPA?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/ucpa/what_reqs_ucpa

Utah consumers are granted a set of data subject rights and consent rights businesses must fulfill. If your business is subject to UCPA, here are the rights you’re legally obligated to enable consumers to exercises.

### VCDPA: What is it and how to comply?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa

Following California’s CPRA, The Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act (CDPA or VCDPA) is the second privacy law to go into effect in 2023. If your business operates in Virginia or targets its products or services to Virginia residents, you’ll need to comply with Virginia’s privacy law.

### VCDPA Step 02: Access Requests for VCDPA
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa/access_requests_vcdpa

Under CPDA, your business must provide consumers with the ability to request access their personal data and respond tho their requests within 45 days. You may also request a 45-day extension for a legitimate reason or if a delay occurs in processing their request.

### Additional Business Obligations of VCDPA
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa/addtl_reqs_vcdpa

VCDPA mandates that businesses must be transparent with their data processing practices. This means businesses must engage in purpose limitation, data minimization, and non-discrimination.

### Conclusion
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa/conclusion_vcdpa

The VCDPA is just one of the many patchwork of U.S. state privacy regulations. Leveraging the privacy engineering expertise of the [Fides open-source community](https://www.ethyca.com), as well as the Fides privacy intelligence platform, will ensure that your business will be able to comply with any global privacy law.

### VCDPA Step 03: Correction Requests for VCDPA
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa/correction_requests_vcdpa

You may already be able to provide consumers with the ability to update the personal information that they believe is incorrect.

### VCPDA Step 01
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa/data_map_vcdpa

While creating a data map is not a strict requirement of VCDPA, a data map is the foundation for compliance with any privacy law. Your business must have full context of all the data you are processing to exert proper control over your organization’s data.

### VCDPA Step 06: Data Protection Assessments
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa/dpa_vcdpa

Virginia’s privacy law requires businesses to perform data protection assessments (DPAs). DPAs are meant for businesses to evaluate the business benefits of processing users' personal data with the potential risks to users. Companies subject to VCDPA should assess the potential risks of:

### VCDPA Step 04: Erasure Requests for VCDPA
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa/erasure_vcdpa

The right to deletion requires the same broad steps as the right to access, but with some additional considerations:

### VCDPA Step 05: Portability Requests for VCDPA
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa/portability_vcdpa

Processing a user’s right to data portability is identical to an access request. The key difference is that the data returned to the user should be in a machine-readable format that could be transferred to another vendor or business.

### What is the VCDPA?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa/what_is_vcdpa

[The Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act (VCDPA)](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacodefull/title59.1/chapter53/) is a comprehensive consumer privacy law that protects the data privacy of all Virginia residents. CDPA went into effect on January 1, 2023, following California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA). Unlike in California, where the enforcement date is July 1, 2023, CDPA’s enforcement date was on the first day of the year.

### What are the requirements of the VCDPA?
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/regulations/vcdpa/what_reqs_vcdpa

Virginia consumers have a host of data subject rights and consent rights businesses need to fulfill. This section will go over these rights in more detail.


## Community

### Join the Fides Community
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community

We believe the only way to solve privacy is as a community of like-minded developers that care to solve these problems for the rest of the world. To make it easier to connect and share ideas, we've created a set of community channels which we'd love to hear from you on:

### Fides Code of Conduct
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/code_of_conduct

In the interest of fostering an open and welcoming environment, we as contributors and maintainers pledge to making participation in our project and our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

### Code Style
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/code_style

Docstrings are required for every function, class, and method. No specific style is required or encouraged, as we expect that most of the relevant information can be gleaned from both the function signature's type-hints as well as descriptive parameter names. The docstring should serve to give additional context/flavour beyond that which can be gained from the code itself.

### Development Tips
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/contributing_details

This page is dedicated to providing further context and information around specific implementation details such as code organization, running migrations and more.

### Database Migration
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/database_migration

Changes to Fides could require a change to the database model. This includes scenarios where you want to persist a new field or replace an existing field. Changes made to the Fides databases are done through alembic migration scripts. Migrations can be found in the following directory: `src/fides/api/alembic/migrations/versions`

### Fides Deploy Development
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/dev_deployment

This guide closely mirrors the [quickstart guide](/getting-started) with some slight differences to account for running in a development environment.

### Documentation
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/documentation

Documentation is an incredibly important part of Fides, both for explaining its concepts to general audiences and describing its usage to developers.

### Analytics
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/fideslog

Fides includes an implementation of [fideslog](https://github.com/ethyca/fideslog) to provide Ethyca with an understanding of user interactions with fides tooling.

### Debugging Fides in IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/jetbrains_debugging

This guide will show how to use the IntelliJ debugger with Fides running in Docker. The setup for PyCharm Professional should be very similar.

### Development Overview
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/overview

Thanks for contributing to Fides! This section of the docs is designed to help you become familiar with how we work, the standards we apply, and how to ensure your contribution is successful.

### Pull Requests
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/pull_requests

Pull requests are the primary unit of work within the Fides project. All code changes are expected to be submitted via a PR with the following requirements:

### Release Checklist
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/release_checklist

The release checklist is a manual set of checks done before each release to ensure functionality of the most critical components of the application. Some of these steps are redundant with automated tests, while others are _only_ tested here as part of this check.

### Releases
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/releases

Fides uses semantic versioning. Due to the rapid development of the project, some minor versions may also contain minor breaking changes. The best practice is to always pin versions, and carefully test before bumping to a new version.

### Testing
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/testing

Fides loves tests! There are a few important reasons to write tests:

### Testing Environment
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/testing_environment

To facilitate thorough manual testing of the application, there is a comprehensive testing environment that can be set up via a single `nox` command.

### community/development/ui
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/ui

To test the UI locally, clone the [FidesOps repository](https://github.com/ethyca/fidesops/), and ensure you have [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) installed to run the application.

### Updating database diagram
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/development/update_erd_diagram

If you make updates to the Fides application database, you should update the DB Architecture diagram in the documentation.

### Community
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/community/hints_tips

The Fides project welcomes issues, contributions and discussion from all users, regardless of background or experience level. In order to create a positive and welcoming environment, all interactions are governed by the Fides [Code of Conduct](/community/code_of_conduct).


## API Reference

### Fides REST API Documentation
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference

Welcome to the Fides REST API documentation. Fides, crafted for developers, offers a simple yet powerful platform for integrating and configuring its features through REST APIs. Navigate to `/docs` in your browser for API access, or visit the [OpenAPI Endpoints](/api-reference/list) page for a complete list.

### API: Authenticating via OAuth
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/auth

The `/api/v1/oauth` routes are a collection of routes that are used to handle Authentication and Authorization within your Fides environment.

### Creating your first OAuth Token
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/auth/generating-tokens

In this section we are going to show you how to get secure access to Fides' API. Fides' API supports the `OAuth2 Client Credentials Grant` which requires you to create a `Client ID` and `Secret` with a specified set of scopes.

### API Documentation
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/list

Fides offers comprehensive APIs to enable developers to integrate any system, database, or SasS with our tooling. Below are our Open Source APIs which can also be found at `/docs` in the browser if running locally. For our Enterprise APIs, please reach out to your Customer Success Manager or run FidesPlus and navigate to `/docs`.

### API: access_manual_webhook
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/access_manual_webhook

The `/api/v1/access_manual_webhook` route lists out all manual webhooks configured within Fides. Manual Webhooks are configured within the [Connection](/api-reference/manage/connection) endpoint.

### API: config
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/config

The `/api/v1/config` routes are a collection of routes that are used to create, update, and delete Fides deployment configuration.

### API: connection
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/connection

The `/api/v1/connection` routes are a collection of routes that are to create, read, update, and delete Connections within Fides. [Database and SaaS Integrations](/integrations) are represented by the `Connection` endpoint on the API level.

### API: connection_type
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/connection_type

The `/api/v1/connection_type` routes are a collection of routes that are used to represent the different types of connections available within the Fides UI. Objects in this endpoint will be represented in the [Integrations UI](/integrations).

### API: consent-request
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/consent-request

The `/api/v1/consent-request` routes are a collection of routes that are used to create, read, and update consent-request objects.

### API: current-privacy-preferences
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/current-privacy-preferences

The `/api/v1/current-privacy-preferences` is designed to give you a report of _current_ consent preferences made by end-user subjects. To see _historical_ preferences, please refer to the [historical-privacy-preferences](/api-reference/manage/historical-privacy-preferences) endpoint.

### API: data_category
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/data_category

The `/api/v1/data_category` routes are used to create, read, update, and delete the [Data Categories](/data-mapping/reference/glossary#data-category) within the Fides platform. Data Categories can be customized but we recommend you use the [Fideslang](https://ethyca.github.io/fideslang/explorer/) taxonomy.

### API: data_qualifier
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/data_qualifier

The `/api/v1/data_qualifier` routes are used to create, read, update, and delete the Data Qualifiers within the Fides platform. Data Qualifiers can be customized but we recommend you use the [Fideslang](https://ethyca.github.io/fideslang/explorer/) taxonomy.

### API: data_subject
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/data_subject

The `/api/v1/data_subject` routes are used to create, read, update, and delete the [Data Subjects](/data-mapping/reference/glossary#data-subject) within the Fides platform. Data Subjects can be customized but we recommend you use the [Fideslang](https://ethyca.github.io/fideslang/explorer/) taxonomy.

### API: data_use
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/data_use

The `/api/v1/data_use` routes are used to create, read, update, and delete the [Data Uses](/data-mapping/reference/glossary#data-use) within the Fides platform. Data Uses can be customized but we recommend you use the [Fideslang](https://ethyca.github.io/fideslang/explorer/) taxonomy.

### API: dataset
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/dataset

The `/api/v1/dataset` routes are a collection of routes that are used to create, read, update and delete [Dataset](/integrations/guides/datasets) objects.

### API: dsr/policy
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/dsr-policy

The `/api/v1/dsr/policy` routes are a collection of routes that are used to [configure Privacy Requests](/privacy-requests). It is important to configure this correctly to properly fulfill [graph traversal](/privacy-requests/concepts/graphs).

### API: dsr/policy/\{policy_key\}/webhook
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/dsr-policy-webhooks

The `/api/v1/dsr/policy/{policy_key}/webhook` routes are a collection of routes that are used to [configure Privacy Requests Webhooks](/privacy-requests/guides/webhooks). This is a powerful tool that allows you to enrich identities (or handle pre/post events) when performing [graph traversal](/privacy-requests/concepts/graphs).

### API: evaluation
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/evaluation

The `/api/v1/evaluation` routes are a collection of routes that are used to create, read, update, and delete [Fides evaluations](/cli-reference/check/cmd-evaluate). This can be used to integrate with popular dashboard and reporting tools to get an overview on repo-level Privacy evaluations within your organization.

### API: experience-config
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/experience-config

The `/api/v1/experience-config` routes are a collection of routes that are used to create, read, update, and delete [Privacy Experience](/consent/concepts/fundamentals/privacy-experiences) configurations.

### API: generate
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/generate

The `/api/v1/generate` routes is a route that performs schema discovery on a Database and generates an _unclassified_ dataset. To generate a classified dataset, you need to have access to the enterprise classifier. If you need access to the classification endpoint, please reach out to your Customer Success Manager or [reach out to us for your enterprise needs](https://www.ethyca.com/speak-with-us?utm_source=docsiteapidocs).

### API: historical-privacy-preferences
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/historical-privacy-preferences

The `/api/v1/historical-privacy-preferences` is designed to give you a report of _historical_ consent preferences made by end-user subjects. To see _current_ preferences, please refer to the [current-privacy-preferences](/api-reference/manage/current-privacy-preferences) endpoint.

### API: login
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/login

The `/api/v1/login` route is used to login to the Fides platform using basic authentication and create a client object on the users behalf simulating a session. It will return identity data as well as an access token.

### API: logout
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/logout

The `/api/v1/logout` route is used to end a session within Fides and remove the client object.

### API: notices-served
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/notices-served

The `/api/v1/notices-served` route records notices served to a Fides's user device id only.

### API: organization
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/organization

The `/api/v1/organization` routes are a collection of routes that are used to define an organization within Fides. By default, the Fides UI uses the default organization, but for advanced use cases, you can use this object as a logical seperator. For most scenarios, you would not need to use this endpoint.

### API: policy
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/policy

The `/api/v1/policy` routes are a collection of routes that are used to create, read, update, and delete Data Map policies that can be used in tandem with [Fides Policy Checks](/cli-reference/check/cmd-evaluate). In the [CI/CD Quickstart](https://fid.es/ci-cd-quickstart?utm_source=docsiteapidocs), we illustrate the policy as a flat YAML file within a repo, however, you can query this endpoint to get the policies dynamically.

### API: privacy-experience
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/privacy-experience

The `/api/v1/privacy-experience` routes is a route that returns a list of [Privacy Experience](/consent/concepts/fundamentals/privacy-experiences) records for individual regions. You can use this endpoint to build a custom privacy experience using our APIs.

### API: Privacy Notice
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/privacy-notice

The `/api/v1/privacy-notice` routes are used to create, read, and update [Privacy Notices](/consent/guides/privacy-notices). You can use this endpoint to create custom Privacy Notice Experiences or integrate into other tooling.

### API: privacy-notice-by-data-use
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/privacy-notice-by-data-use

The `/api/v1/privacy-notice-by-data-use` route provides a mapping of [Data Uses](/api-reference/manage/data_use) to [Privacy Notices](/api-reference/manage/privacy-notice). You can use this endpoint for building custom privacy experiences.

### API: privacy-preferences
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/privacy-preferences

The `/api/v1/privacy-preferences` route records privacy preferences saved for a user by using Fides's user device id only.

### API: privacy-request
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/privacy-request

The `/api/v1/privacy-request` are a collection of routes that create, read, and update [Privacy Requests](/privacy-requests/concepts/fundamentals) and related actions. You can use these endpoints to create a custom Privacy Request experience.

### Privacy Request Redaction Patterns API
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/privacy-request-redaction-patterns

The Privacy Request Redaction Patterns API allows you to manage global regex patterns that automatically mask sensitive dataset, collection, and field names in DSR (Data Subject Request) package reports.

### API: registration
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/registration

The `/api/v1/registration` routes show the Fides registration status with Ethyca.

### API: registry
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/registry

The `/api/v1/registry` routes are a collection of routes that are used create, read, update, and delete registry objects.

### API: system
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/system

The `/api/v1/system` routes are a collection of routes that are used to create system entries within your Fides environment. A System is the highest-level object in Fides that encapsulates `Data Uses` (Privacy Declarations object), Tags, Metadata around Data Responsibilities, [Data Categories/Uses](/api-reference/manage/data_use), and optionally [Datasets](/api-reference/manage/dataset). Note, you can also instanciate a [Connection](/api-reference/manage/connection) (also known as an [Integration](/privacy-requests/guides/configuration/integrations) in the UI)

### API: user
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/user

The `/api/v1/user` routes are a collection of routes that are used to create, read, update, and delete user objects within your Fides tenant. A user can also have Role-Based-Access-Control (RBAC) for specific systems using the `system-manager` endpoints. This might be known as Data Stewards for larger organizations.

### API: Validate
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/api-reference/manage/validate

The `/api/v1/validate` routes are a collection of routes that are used to validate different resource targets.


## CLI Reference

### Fides CLI Documentation
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference

Learn Fides' CLI-based workflows. You can use the CLI to interact with the Fides Server.

### Authenticating & Managing Users via CLI
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/auth

Fides is a platform that performs automated privacy tasks, offering a collaboration-focused environment that makes it easier for teams to quickly comply with privacy together.

### Command: user create
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/auth/cmd-create

The ```fides user create``` command can be used to create a new user on the Fides Server.

### Command: user login
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/auth/cmd-login

The ```fides user login``` command can be used to automatically obtain and save an access token for Fides Server.

### Command: user permissions
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/auth/cmd-permissions

The ```fides user permissions``` command can be used to list the scopes available for the currently logged in user.

### Automated Privacy Checks
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/check

One of the main benefits of Fides is to speed up and simplify data cataloging and data inventory management with tools built for data annotation. Fides' annotations include all of the information necessary to ensure compliance with global privacy and data governance regulations. A key part of compliance is ensuring that all data is adequately labeled.

### Command: evaluate
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/check/cmd-evaluate

The ```fides evaluate``` performs an automated privacy check on any change to a resource to ensure they comply with Fides policies.

### Basic CLI Features
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/cli-basics

The command line interface to Fides is the ```fides``` command, which accepts a variety of subcommands such as ```fides init``` or ```fides generate```.

### Fides Configuration
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/config

Fides can be configured in two different ways: either via a ```toml``` file or via environment variables. Both methods can be used simultaneously, with environment variables taking precedence over the ```toml``` file values.

### Command: view
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/config/cmd-view

The ```fides view``` command prints the current configuration of the Fides instance.

### Connecting CLI to Fides Cloud
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/fides-cloud/connecting-cli-to-fides-cloud

In this guide, we will setup the Fides CLI on your local machine and connect it to your Fides Cloud instance so that you can programmatically push & pull resources, evaluate privacy checks, and much more!

### Initializing Fides Configuration Files
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/init

Fides can be configured in two different ways: either via a ```toml``` file or via environment variables. Both methods can be used simultaneously, with environment variables taking precedence over the ```toml``` file values.

### Command: init
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/init/cmd-init

> **Hands-on:** Try the [Fides Quick Start](/getting-started). For more in-depth details on the ```init``` command, check out the [Initialize Fides Configuration tutorial](/cli-reference/init).

### Managing Privacy Resources with Fides
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/manage

Fides' primary function is to create and maintain datasets that can be used to automate compliance tasks for global privacy regulations.

### Command: annotate
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/manage/cmd-annotate

The `fides annotate` starts an interactive shell that provides a guided flow for annotating datasets manually. Dataset annotation in Fides relies on identifying and labeling sensitive data using the Fides taxonomy. For more in-depth details on sensitive data and the Fides taxonomy, see the [Fides Sensitive Data Taxonomy](https://ethyca.github.io/fideslang/explorer/) guide.

### Command: delete
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/manage/cmd-delete

The ```fides delete``` command deletes a remote resource completely from the Fides Server.

### Command: generate
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/manage/cmd-generate

The ```fides generate``` command is a multipurpose tool used to connect to a specified database/service and automatically generate Fides resources in the Fides YAML format and style. This command generates a YAML resource file based on the data source's schema. By default the documents generated by this command are written to the ```.fides``` working directory.

### Command: get
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/manage/cmd-get

The ```fides get``` command retrieves the specified resources from the Fides Server and outputs the repsonse in YAML.

### Command: ls
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/manage/cmd-ls

The ```fides ls``` command gets a list of all resources from the server and displays them as YAML.

### Command: parse
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/manage/cmd-parse

The ```fides parse``` validates the syntax of all local resources in the ```.fides``` working directory and outputs any errors to the CLI.

### Command: pull
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/manage/cmd-pull

The ```fides pull``` command updates local resources in the ```.fides``` working directory to match those on the server.

### Command: push
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/manage/cmd-push

The ```fides push``` validates the syntax and structure of the Fides YAML documents in the working directory before persisting those validated documents to the Fides Server. This is ideal for centralizing resources and collaboration with other teams.

### Exporting Reports from Fides
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/report

One of Fides' most powerful features is the ability to export reports for compliance with multiple global privacy regulations including the GDPR in Europe, the CCPA in California, the LGPD in Brazil, and PIPL in China. Reports can be generated from both the CLI and the Fides UI. For more in-depth details on reporting, check out the [Building and Exporting Reports in Fides](/data-mapping/guides/reports) tutorials.

### Command: export
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/report/cmd-export

> **Hands-on:** Try the [Building and Exporting Reports in Fides](/data-mapping/guides/reports) tutorials.

### Learning with the Fides "Cookie House" Sample Project
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/sample

Fides comes packaged with a sample project, called the "Cookie House". The Cookie House is fictional e-commerce store designed to simulate a real application. The Cookie House can be used to test and quickly learn many of Fides' core features and workflows of the CLI and UI.

### Command: deploy
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/sample/cmd-deploy

> **Hands-on:** Try the [Fides Quick Start](/getting-started) guide.

### Checking Annotation Coverage
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/scan

One of the main benefits of Fides is to speed up and simplify data cataloguing and data inventory management with tools built for data annotation. Fides' annotations include all of the information necessary to ensure compliance with global privacy and data governance regulations. A key part of compliance is ensuring that all data is adequately labeled.

### Command: scan
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/scan/cmd-scan

> **Hands-on:** Try the [Fides Quick Start](/getting-started). For more in-depth details on the ```scan``` command, check out the [Annotation Coverage tutorial](/integrations/guides/datasets).

### Task Management in Fides with Workers
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/task

Fides is a powerful data orchestration engine for privacy tasks such as deleting or retrieving user data across systems. Often completing these data privacy tasks requires asynchronous execution across multiple distributed systems and as the volume of these requests grow it may create challenges in request processing.

### Command: worker
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/task/cmd-worker

> **Hands-on:** To understand workers in Fides, see the [Worker reference](/platform/workers).

### Running Fides Webserver
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/webserver

The Fides CLI integrates with the Fides Server to provide a central solution for collaboration on privacy and data governance tasks for teams.

### Command: db
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/webserver/cmd-db

The ```fides db``` is the database utility that supports initialization and resetting of the database Fides.

### Command: status
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/webserver/cmd-status

The ```fides status``` makes a request to the Fides server to check its health, current version and report back any possible issues.

### Command: webserver
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/cli-reference/webserver/cmd-webserver

The ```fides webserver``` starts the Fides webserver using the available configuration and environment variables. By default, when Fides starts the webserver it:

## Other

### About Ethyca
URL: https://www.ethyca.com/docs/ethyca

The mission of Ethyca is to make Internet-scale technology respectful and ethical. We're a venture-backed privacy technology team headquartered in New York, but working as a distributed team across the US to solve what we believe is the most important problem in technology today: the human right to privacy in vastly complex data-driven systems.
